articles.title: Beat Up Truck
articles.summary: Smooth semi-matte surface with faint dents and scuff marks, like a work truck that has taken a beating but still shines a little. Looks like a plain semi-matte painted truck in whatever colour you give it; the wear is too faint to read at distance.
articles.what: Up close: Takes your colour: the paint itself is flat, with no visible dents or scuffs in the picture. The only structure is a faint soft roughness mottle in the spec strips, vertical smudges a few hundred pixels tall, stretched here to show up; the real spec swing is tiny (R std 6). From a distance: Looks like a plain semi-matte painted truck in whatever colour you give it; the wear is too faint to read at distance. Measured spec (average): metal 50, roughness 154, coat 160. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: low. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: truck / off-road, dirt late model, stock car.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put Beat Up Truck on the hood".
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Any panel: it is a quiet semi-matte base
Bumpers and body sides work well with added wear overlays
Flat colour with no texture, so numbers read cleanly in any contrasting colour.
Rust, scratch and dirt overlays: this base is flat, so the wear has to come from the pattern
Pairs well with: rust brown, olive, cream, black.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not a dented panel texture: the render shows no dents, only a flat colour
Not rusty: it takes your colour, no rust colour is added
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to other loud finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 50 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 154 (semi-matte), clearcoat 160 (dull or trace clearcoat).
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Gloss shows the paint colour as it is, so any colour works; pick the colour for contrast with the neighbouring zones, not for the finish. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to other loud finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: rust, scratch and dirt overlays: this base is flat, so the wear has to come from the pattern; worn-edge or chip patterns: give the beat-up story that the spec cannot
Patterns to avoid: shiny glitter or flake patterns: contradict the dull worn base; clean pinstripes: look new on an old base
Spec overlays that work: scratch or abrasion spec patterns: add the missing roughness wear; chip or scuff spec patterns: add dents-and-scuff variation in the shine
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Beetle Jewel
articles.summary: Dense multicolour sparkle confetti, tiny iridescent flecks of pink, blue, green and gold on dark base. A dusky purple-magenta speckle with dark gaps and warm gold flecks; reads as a dark colourful confetti, mostly plum.
articles.what: Up close: Tight mosaic of small angular cells, 6-10 px, in muted violet, magenta, blue, olive-gold, orange and the odd green, with black cells mixed in. Each cell is flat with a soft edge, like crushed gem chips or stained-glass confetti. From a distance: A dusky purple-magenta speckle with dark gaps and warm gold flecks; reads as a dark colourful confetti, mostly plum. Measured spec (average): metal 44, roughness 99, coat 100. Shine: satin. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, hero panel, roof.
Fits: show car, gt / sports car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Beetle Jewel" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and sides: fine mosaic works on any big panel
Trim loses the cells
Mosaic noise hurts thin numbers; bold white or yellow numbers with a black outline read.
Almost nothing: the mosaic is already busy
Pairs well with: black, chrome, white, deep purple.
pitfalls: Not smooth iridescent beetle paint: it is hard flat mosaic cells
Not Beetle Elytra: that is a banded bumpy shell, this is random confetti
Avoid: small numbers over busy flake, next to other loud finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 44 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 99 (satin gloss), clearcoat 100 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers over busy flake, next to other loud finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: almost nothing: the mosaic is already busy; a large soft fade or panel block of solid black beside it
Patterns to avoid: any flake or glitter pattern: noise on noise; camo or weave: drowned
Spec overlays that work: gloss clear: deepens the cell colours; leave spec alone: it already has strong metal variation
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
